principle: Derive the Plan from the Pawn Structure
rule: Read the fixed pawn skeleton before choosing where to maneuver or attack.
Decide which exchange improves the resulting position before maneuvering to make it happen.

principle: Activate the King in a Quiet Middlegame
rule: When queens are off and tactics permit, improve the king before the formal endgame begins.

principle: Create the Entry Square Before Taking the File
rule: An open file matters only if your heavy pieces can enter the opponent's position through it.
Double rooks or invade only when doing so creates a concrete target, tie-down, or favorable exchange.

principle: Distinguish a Weak Square from an Outpost
rule: Call a square an outpost only when a piece can occupy it safely and do useful work there.

principle: Control the Break Before Starting the Attack
rule: Prevent or answer the opponent's freeing pawn break before committing pieces elsewhere.
Take away the opponent's active breaks and piece routes before attacking fixed weaknesses.
When one weakness is fully defended, create a second weakness far from it.
Place pieces on central routes before transferring the attack from one flank to the other.
Attack squares of the color the opponent can no longer contest effectively.
When cramped, consider exchanges or pawn breaks that concede territory but leave attackable pawns.
In the Carlsbad structure, compare the minority attack with a central e-pawn break before committing.

principle: Use the IQP Before It Becomes Weak
rule: With an isolated queen's pawn, exploit activity and prepare the d5 advance while pieces remain on the board.
Move one hanging pawn only when the advance gains space, creates a passer, or supports a concrete break.
Use the Maroczy structure to restrain ...d5, but keep improving pieces and preparing your own break.

principle: Choose Between e5 and f5 in the Benoni
rule: Select the central or kingside break according to piece support and the opponent's blockade.

principle: Attack the King's Indian Chain at Its Base
rule: Use c5 or related queenside breaks against the base of the central pawn chain while monitoring the kingside race.
In the French structure, challenge White's e5 pawn with ...f6 only when the center and king can withstand opening lines.

principle: Use Caro-Kann Structure in the Endgame
rule: Exploit the sound pawn base and challenge White's space before accepting passive defense.
In a Hedgehog, prepare ...b5 or ...d5 until the tactical release gains maximum force.
Use the protected central knight as the active center of the Stonewall plan and support its routes.

principle: Use the Open Files Around an Isolated c-Pawn
rule: Balance the isolated c-pawn's weakness against the activity provided by adjacent open files.

principle: Advance a Majority with Pieces Behind It
rule: Support a pawn majority from behind before creating a passed pawn.
Before exchanging pawns, compare the new islands, files, weak squares, and endgame—not just the immediate capture.
